paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the God who hears your prayers is the same God who runs the whole world. David calls Him "O You who listen to prayer" (Psalm 65:2), and in the same song he says God formed the mountains "by Your power" (Psalm 65:6). Nobody has to pick between a God who is close and a God who is big. David sings about both in one breath.

Look at what David does with honesty, too. He says "When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions" (Psalm 65:3). He doesn't pretend. He says it plain, and then he says what God does about it. Then he calls the one God brings near "blessed" (Psalm 65:4), and I spent years in a junk drawer, so believe me, being brought near is a BIG deal.

And then the song comes down to the dirt. God waters the earth, prepares the grain, and "You crown the year with Your bounty" (Psalm 65:11). Rain on a field, food on a table, a good season: David sees God in all of it, and the hills and valleys end up shouting and singing (Psalm 65:13). So the next time you eat a meal or feel the rain, friend, let it send you to praise. The ordinary stuff is where He's been showing up all along.
